proof_summary: Writing \(v=v_2(\varphi(m))\), a prime-factor induction shows that any \(m<2^{v+1}\) is a squarefree product of Fermat primes \(F_j\), with \(v=\sum_{j\in S}2^j\); the size bound rules out a factor of \(2\), higher odd prime powers, and odd primes for which \(p-1\) has a nontrivial odd part. For an admissible \(m<2^{N+1}\), where \(N=2^{33}\), product bounds force \(v=N\), so uniqueness of binary expansion gives \(S=\{33\}\); meanwhile \(\varphi(m)<m\) gives the lower bound \(m>2^N\), and \(2^{N+1}\) supplies the fallback candidate.
